text:
maria: Heads-up — after the latest kernel selector change (auto-fit v2) we're seeing a small but consistent tail latency bump on the reranker embeddings endpoint (non-chat workloads).
aj: saw that in dashboards. p95 up ~30-40ms on 1s jobs?
maria: yep, p95 +35ms, p99 closer to +120ms on heavy 64k token-batch mixes. throughput steady.
tim: interesting — throughput steady suggests kernel runtime is slower on some sequences; could be worse vectorized math path for short sequences?
jen: I pulled a perf profile from a repro run on staging: attached traces show extra memcpy + kernel fallback path when batch shape mismatches quantized-accel kernels.
jen: pasted stack snippet:
```
KernelSelector::select() -> fallback_to_generic_kernel()
runtime::run_kernel_generic -> launch_cuda_kernel
memcpy(Device->Host) // unexpected for small KV hits
```
sahil: kv-cache hit rate dropped ~7% during the window, maybe because batching grouped diverse prefixes so KV cache lookups misaligned with shard keys.
maria: good catch. If KV cache locality decreases, we could be incurring additional mem transfers and kernel-choice jitter.
aj: what if we tweak batch formation to prefer homogeneous sequence-length buckets for rerankers? smaller bucket variance should help kernel-match ratio.
tim: agree. Also consider a token-budget target per batch shape: cap tokens per batch variant so we don't force huge shape diversity. Example config idea:
```
batching:
  shapes:
    - max_tokens: 8192
      max_items: 32
      length_stddev_threshold: 12
    - max_tokens: 16384
      max_items: 16
      length_stddev_threshold: 6
```
jen: also we should adjust queue policy: prefer draining older batches that already have homogeneous candidates rather than waiting to fill with heterogeneous inflight requests. That reduces churn.
sahil: we can add a 'kv-affinity' flag when enqueuing: route requests with same doc-shard id to preferred batch shards to improve cache hits. low-risk toggle for canary.
maria: sounds good. action items: 1) tim/jen run a kernel selector sim with sequence-homogenous batching to measure kernel-fit rate. 2) aj/sahil try kv-affinity flag in staging and capture p95/p99 + kv-hit stats. 3) deploy token-budget caps as quick config change.

infra-bot: deploy request created: canary/rerank-emb-batcher-kv-affinity -> staging (PR #4523).
aj: I'll own the canary deploy, will run a 4h synthetic with mixed lengths and a production-like arrival trace.
tim: if we see kernel fallback path drop < 2% and p99 improves, we can roll to prod. If fallback still >5% we'll revert and iterate.
jen: I'll attach profiler before/after and a short log parser to count kernel selection IDs per batch.
sahil: one more note — caching changes might interact with our prefetcher. add prefetch skip on kv-affinity to avoid double work.
maria: thanks team. please post back with numbers in this thread. i'll update the runbook if we flip this to prod. :thumbsup:
jen: quick note — I also saw a tiny memory spike on one node (staging-3) during the test, probably due to holding larger per-batch buffers; watch OOM logs.
aj: noted. will watch alerts.
maria: closing loop: if results are good, we'll include these heuristics in the continuous-batching guide and add a perf regression test targeting reranker endpoints.
jen: cool. syncing with infra in 30m.
aj: starting canary now. will report back at ~1767771389 when first stable window completes.
